name: Manor of Cardross
summary: The residence near where Robert the Bruce died in 1329.
overview: The Manor of Cardross was a royal residence near the River Clyde associated with Robert the Bruce’s final years.
Bruce died there in 1329 after securing a stronger Scottish monarchy.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Cardross near the Clyde estuary in Scotland was a royal manor where Robert the Bruce spent his final years and died in June 1329. The manor was his preferred residence during his last period of illness.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Robert's death at Cardross ended the reign of the king who had secured Scottish independence through the Declaration of Arbroath (1320) and the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton (1328), by which England recognized Scottish sovereignty. His heart was removed after death and taken on crusade by James Douglas, part of a tradition of vow-fulfillment by proxy.
